chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Qazzāz, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, “Why was he named Amīr al-Muʾminīn?”
He said, “Allah named him, and thus did He reveal in His Book:”

“And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: Am I not your Lord? And that Muḥammad is My Messenger, and that ʿAlī is Amīr al-Muʾminīn.”

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful; the divinely designated title of ʿAlī عليه السلام in this narration
key_terms.أَنْزَلَ: revealed; indicating divine revelation in the Book
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who bestowed this title according to the hadith
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ: their descendants; the offspring of Banī Ādam brought forth for testimony
key_terms.رَبُّكَ: your Lord; referring to Allah in the covenant scene
key_terms.عَلِيًّا: ʿAlī; identified here with the title Amīr al-Muʾminīn
key_terms.كِتَابِهِ: His Book; the revealed scripture in which this meaning is stated
key_terms.مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولِي: Muḥammad is My Messenger; affirmation of the Messenger’s divine mission

ai.seo_question: Why is ʿAlī عليه السلام called Amīr al-Muʾminīn in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the title Amīr al-Muʾminīn for ʿAlī عليه السلام was bestowed by Allah and connected to the primordial covenant taken from the progeny of Ādam. It presents the recognition of Allah’s lordship together with the mission of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the authority of ʿAlī عليه السلام as part of a divinely established testimony.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Raie Al Qazzaz, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Why is Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> named as such?’

like this it is Revealed in Hisazwj Book [7:172] And when your Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants, and made them testify against their own souls: Am I not your Lord, and Muhammadsaww is My Rasool and Aliasws is Amir Al-Momineen?’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from ya‘qub ibn Yazid from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al-Rabi‘ al-Qazzaz from Jabir who has said the following.
“I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.), ‘Why is he (Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) is called Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.)?”
He said, “Allah has given him this name and as such it has come in His book,

“When your Lord asked all the offspring of Adam (before their birth), “Am I not your Lord?” All of them testified and bore witness to their testimony that on the Day of Judgment they would not say, “We were not aware of this (fact),.” [7:172] that Muhammad is My messenger and Ali is Amir al-Mu’minin (commander of the faithful).”
